ideas.title: Your Phone Motion Sensor Is a Hidden Spy
ideas.angle: Explain that malicious websites use your phone's tilt sensors to reconstruct what you're typing. Includes a challenge for the viewer to rotate their phone to see a visual simulation of the data flow, prompting them to comment their phone model for a 'security rating'.

hook.en: Stop typing until you flip your phone.

ideas.reason: Privacy-focused tech shorts are peaking due to recent zero-click exploit news. This specific angle uses the 'Interactive' archetype by making the viewer physically move their device, boosting retention.
sources: Newcastle University Research on Accelerometer Keystroke Logging
MIT Technology Review: How sensors leak your data

ideas.title: The Creepy Way AI Detects Lies
ideas.angle: Reveals that your pupils dilate by 0.5mm when you lie, and phone cameras can now track this in real-time. Challenges the viewer to stare into their camera lens and blink twice to 'recalibrate', which forces a 100%+ rewatch as they try the test.

hook.en: Look into your camera right now.

ideas.reason: The 'Bizarre Body Science' combined with 'AI Secret' is a high-velocity hybrid. Viewers are obsessed with how AI interacts with their biological responses.
sources: Journal of Nonverbal Behavior: Pupil Dilation and Deception

ideas.title: Why You Shouldn't Book Flights with Low Battery
ideas.angle: Explains how travel apps use your battery percentage to detect desperation and raise prices. Forces engagement by asking viewers to 'Type your battery percentage' in the comments to see if they're currently being targeted for higher prices.

hook.en: Never book flights with low battery.

ideas.reason: The 'Hidden Money Traps' pillar combined with a 'forbidden' tech secret triggers immediate urgency and high comment volume via the battery percentage call-to-action.
sources: Princeton University Study on Dark Patterns in E-commerce
Data Privacy Lab: Battery Status API Exploitation
